SMTO-TSK-0065 — The Agent's plan for several steps was rejected

GUID: cfdcedde-b45b-4479-8c5c-aabddde9d36a
Slug: dependency-arguments-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent asked to run a group of steps together, but the request for the whole group had a problem, so SMTO turned it down. None of the steps in that group ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the rejected step in the conversation to read the reason shown for it. The reason tells you, and the Agent, what was wrong with the group request.
  2. Wait to see whether the Agent tries again with a corrected request; it is told about this problem automatically. The Agent usually fixes the request on its next attempt.
  3. If the task ends with this error, send a message asking the Agent to continue and do the steps one at a time. None of the grouped steps ran, so asking again won't repeat any work.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's steps start and show results in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it is likely to be grouped the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Dependency-graph validation stopped because the parent schedule_activities or parallel call had already been rejected (a non-reused rejection result), so its error, or the fallback parent-invalid message, was applied to the whole batch before any child was admitted.

What this means

  • A dependency-graph parent already carries a non-reused rejection result; validation propagates its error or the fallback parent-invalid message before admitting children. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A dependency-graph parent already carries a non-reused rejection result; validation propagates its error or the fallback parent-invalid message before admitting children.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original parent's specific rejection and distinguish it from any separately retained reused receipt.

How to fix it

  • Read the parent call's rejection in the tool activity (the original error is propagated) and correct its arguments, for example the schedule_activities structure or targets. Children are never admitted from a rejected parent; resubmit a corrected batch rather than the same arguments.
  • Inspect the parent rejection and correct its operation arguments before submitting the batch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended parent request validates and its children pass their own admission checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
